data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'petra,' meaning rock or stone. In the Bible, Jesus describes Himself as the Rock of Ages, a firm foundation upon which believers can build their lives. The name Rock carries the meaning “Firm foundation” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Rock usually hope their child will grow to embody firm foundation and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of steadfastness and unwavering faith
data.etymology: Rock belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Firm foundation.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rock total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The term "rock" in popular culture has come to symbolize an enduring foundation, a solid and unchanging force. It can also represent music genres, including Rock 'n' Roll, which emerged in the late 1940s and 1950s and has since defined generations through its oppositional and rebellious spirit. "Rock and roll" continues to evoke images of freedom, excitement, and self-expression.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian theology, Jesus is referred to as the "Rock of Ages" (later popularized in a hymn of the same name by Augustus Toplady), emphasizing the eternal, unyielding nature of God. The metaphor of a rock is used throughout scripture, such as in Deuteronomy 32:3, where God is described as the 'rock' that took care of Israel in the wilderness. This biblical symbolism highlights the idea of a steadfast and unchanging God, providing comfort and security for believers in their spiritual journeys.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Rock carries profound spiritual symbolism as it is rooted in Biblical tradition.
